blocks.text: What an AI assistant for account executives does on a Mac

Most AI tools start with writing. Account executives need help with reading first. You want to know what a buyer asked, where the pricing link sits, what was agreed on the last call and what to say next. That is reading and finding work, and it runs across Gmail, Outlook, Slack and your CRM all day. An AI assistant for account executives earns its place when it can see that work and answer about it.

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. You hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask about anything on your screen. Lazur answers out loud. If you ask where something is, it draws a circle and a label around it. If you ask how to do something, it guides you one click at a time and waits for each click. It does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you.
Voice assistant for sales reps on Mac: the limits

A voice assistant for sales reps on Mac can read your screen, explain it, point at things, draft text and dictate. It cannot send email for you or update your CRM. Plan your week around those limits, and keep the final click yours.
Where an account executive's day goes

Salesforce's State of Sales 2026 survey asked 4,050 sales professionals how they spend their time. Sellers reported about 40% of their time on active selling. Salesforce's Dictionary article calls the remaining 60% administrative drag. That includes data entry, internal meetings, content searching, manual forecasting and follow-up admin.

Read that number with care. It is self-reported survey data, not time tracking. The survey was double-anonymous and ran from August through September 2025. It is still a useful baseline for your own week. Compare it with a week you track yourself.

Salesforce also reports that Gen Z reps lose about two hours each week to manual data entry. It says nearly one full day of the workweek goes to prospecting. Those two lines point to where an assistant saves the most time. Data entry and research both start with reading something on screen.
Why email and chat never let up

Microsoft's 2025 Work Trend Index follow-up says the average knowledge worker gets 117 emails a day. Most are skimmed in under 60 seconds. The same report counts 153 Teams messages per weekday and 275 interruptions a day from meetings, emails or chats. Those figures cover knowledge workers in general.

No study isolates account executives. Treat these numbers as a pattern, not as your own count. Still, if your inbox looks like that, a faster way to find the question matters more than a faster way to type. Pull up last week and count the threads that needed an answer.

blocks.text: The BLS figure is the closest official category, not an exact match for account executives. It projects little or no change in employment for wholesale and manufacturing sales reps from 2025 to 2035. Flat headcount does not mean lighter workloads. The admin work stays on the desk either way.

Asana's Anatomy of Work Index, based on over 10,000 knowledge workers, puts 60% of work time on what it calls work about work. That covers communicating about work, searching for information, switching apps and chasing status. It is vendor research, so read it as a direction, not a precise measure.
AI help for account executive email on your Mac

Start with the thread, not the reply. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask what the buyer needs before you type anything. Lazur reads the messages on your screen and answers out loud. That takes seconds, and it beats scrolling back through a long chain to find the last question.
Find the open question in a long thread

Long threads hide the one question that blocks the deal. The buyer's last message often asks something new. Ask Lazur for the open questions, in the order they were asked. Then ask where the newest one sits. Lazur circles it, so you read it in context and not in a summary.

If buyer mail buries your inbox, sort it first. Our guide on [creating a filter in Gmail](/how-to/create-a-filter-in-gmail) shows the browser steps. Filters keep buyer threads in one place, so the open question does not get lost under newsletters.
Add the right people to CC without guessing

A missing manager on CC, or an internal note sent to a buyer, can cost a deal. Gmail on the web shows CC and BCC in the compose window. The browser steps and shortcuts are in our [CC and BCC guide](/how-to/add-cc-and-bcc-in-gmail). If you forget where a field lives, ask Lazur to walk you through it.
Check the reply before you send

items: Read the last few messages, not only the newest one.
Check the To and CC lines against the buyer's team.
Read back any price, date or product name you dictated.
Confirm every number in a draft against your quote.
Check your employer's rules before pasting customer details into any tool.

blocks.text: Those checks take less time than a correction email. The last item matters most. Customer data needs your company's approval before it goes into an AI tool, even on your own Mac.
Outlook, Apple Mail and Gmail steps on your Mac

Check your email app before you follow any steps. Microsoft's Outlook for Mac help says you turn on the new Outlook by turning off the Legacy Outlook switch. Accounts do not carry over between new and legacy. To go back, use Help > Revert to Legacy Outlook.

Microsoft's page says support for legacy Outlook for Mac ends in October 2026. That month has already passed. Support also depends on your Microsoft 365, Office or Outlook license. Confirm the details with Microsoft, because third-party sites give different dates.

blocks.title: Legacy Outlook deadline
blocks.text: If you still run legacy Outlook for Mac, the published support window has closed. Ask your IT team which version your account uses before you rely on it for customer mail.

Apple Mail has its own guide. Apple's Mail User Guide for Mac covers writing and sending email, search, notifications, automatic sorting into mailboxes, attachments, spam and keyboard shortcuts. The guide is labeled for macOS 27. Search it for the shortcut you need, then ask Lazur to point at the control on screen.
Gmail in a browser works the same way. Lazur reads the page you have open in Safari or Chrome. For the browser steps, see our [Gmail page for account executives](/for/account-executives/gmail).
Account executive Slack and deal channels

Slack holds much of the deal talk. Give each deal or account its own channel, so the context stays in one place. Our [Slack page for account executives](/for/account-executives/slack) covers setup and shortcuts. For the channel steps, see [creating a channel in Slack](/how-to/create-a-channel-in-slack).

blocks.title: Check your Slack version
blocks.text: Slack's support lifecycle page lists app versions 4.46.104 and below as end of support on November 9, 2026. That date is tomorrow. Update the Mac app today.

Hold ⌥ ⌘ in Slack and ask what changed in a busy channel since the morning. Lazur answers out loud. Treat that answer as a summary, not a record. Read the channel before you promise anything to a buyer.
Research before a sales call, and how to check it

Research saves the most reading time. Lazur runs research in its own Chrome tabs, through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It comes back with a summary and a report. Skim the report first, then open the sources it used before you rely on a single line.

items: Name the company and the one fact you need, such as its latest announcement.
Ask for the sources the report used, then open at least two of them.
Check names, titles and dates against the company's own site.
Copy the lines you will use into a note before the call.

blocks.text: Research tools can miss news or mix up two companies with similar names. Verify the one fact that would change your pitch. A wrong report costs more time than the research saved, so check before you walk in.
Dictation for follow-ups and call notes

Hold fn to dictate. Lazur turns your speech into clean, formatted text at the cursor, in any app. Use it for a Gmail follow-up, a Slack reply or a CRM note. Snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots handle the words you repeat, such as product names and your sign-off.

Speak prices, seat counts and dates slowly. Those are the words where one small error costs you most. Read the text back before you send it. To see how much speaking could save you, try the [speaking versus typing test](/tools/speaking-vs-typing-test).
Customer data, privacy and your employer's rules

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Those are the product details. They describe how Lazur handles a request, not what your company allows.

blocks.title: Your employer's rules come first
blocks.text: Your employer sets the rules for customer data. Check the policy before you paste a buyer's contract, pricing sheet or personal details into any AI tool. This page makes no compliance claims for Lazur.
If your security team needs a review, send them Lazur's privacy details first. Let them decide what your team may share. Your job is to ask before you paste, not after.
Mistakes account executives make with AI help

items: Trusting a summary without opening the thread. Summaries drop tone, and tone matters in a stalled deal.
Asking vague questions. Ask for the open pricing question, not 'what happened'.
Sending dictated numbers unread. Speech tools can mishear prices and dates.
Forgetting to hold the key. Lazur only listens and looks while you hold the shortcut.
Running old app versions. Check your Slack version and your Outlook setup.
Pasting customer data into any tool without checking your employer's rules.

blocks.text: Most of these come down to one habit. Read the source, ask a narrow question and check the numbers. That takes seconds. It also keeps your name on the email, and your credibility with the buyer.

faq.question: Is there an AI assistant for account executives that works in any Mac app?
faq.answer: Lazur is an AI assistant for the Mac that works with whatever is on your screen. You hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about what you see, and it answers out loud. It is not a plugin or add-in for any app, and it has no partnership with any app maker.

faq.question: Does Lazur send emails, update the CRM or click buttons for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It guides you one click at a time, and it drafts text and types it where you ask. You send, save and update everything yourself.

faq.question: Can Lazur run on Windows?
faq.answer: Lazur runs on macOS, on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available yet.

faq.question: How much time can an AI assistant save an account executive?
faq.answer: No study measures this for account executives. Salesforce's State of Sales 2026 survey says sellers expect AI agents to cut prospect research time by 34% and email drafting by 36%. Those are expectations, not measured results. Test the claim against your own week.

faq.question: Is my customer data safe with Lazur?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Your employer's rules on customer data still apply, and this page makes no compliance claims.
